architecture_rules.text: Feature modules must not import from other feature modules.
architecture_rules.why: Cross-feature imports tie features together, so one feature cannot be changed or removed without breaking another.
architecture_rules.note: Instruction only until a project has a features folder (campaign decision 4.4): the scaffold creates none, so there is no path for a linter zone to name. A no-restricted-paths zone per feature would make it a validator.

architecture_rules.text: Code under src/ outside src/lib/supabase/ and outside test files must not create a Supabase client (createClient, createBrowserClient, createServerClient from the Supabase packages); it uses the helpers in src/lib/supabase/.
architecture_rules.why: One place builds the Supabase client, so session handling, keys and typing are configured once and a component cannot reach the database around the helpers.

paths.name: @supabase/supabase-js
paths.message: Use the helpers in src/lib/supabase/ instead of creating a client here.

paths.name: @supabase/ssr
paths.message: Use the helpers in src/lib/supabase/ instead of creating a client here.

architecture_rules.note: Restricts the client factories of the two packages by name, so type imports (User, Session, SupabaseClient) stay allowed; a namespace import of either package is flagged. Static imports only: dynamic import() and require() are not caught. A name pattern across all modules is deliberately absent: it would flag every `import * as React`, and helpers may be called createClient. Session-refresh code for Next.js middleware also belongs in src/lib/supabase/ (a helper that src/middleware.ts calls). A per-line disable with a reason is the grandfathering mechanism.

architecture_rules.text: Components must not call fetch(); external API calls go through src/lib/api/.
architecture_rules.why: A single API layer owns URLs, headers, error handling and typing, so components stay free of transport details and a call can be mocked in one place.

no-restricted-globals.name: fetch
no-restricted-globals.message: Call the API through src/lib/api/ instead of fetch() in a component.

no-restricted-properties.message: Call the API through src/lib/api/ instead of fetch() in a component.
Call the API through src/lib/api/ instead of fetch() in a component.

architecture_rules.note: Scope is src/components/** and the .tsx/.jsx files under src/app/**; route handlers (route.ts) are not components and stay out of scope. Metadata image files (opengraph-image, twitter-image, icon) are ignored because they fetch fonts and assets; hooks outside src/components are out of scope. A legitimate exception takes a per-line disable with a reason.

architecture_rules.text: Components are Server Components by default; add 'use client' only when state, effects or browser APIs are needed.
architecture_rules.why: Server Components send less JavaScript to the browser and fetch data next to where it is rendered.
architecture_rules.note: Whether a component needs the browser is a design call, not a pattern a linter can decide.

architecture_rules.text: API routes validate input, check authentication and delegate; business logic lives in Edge Functions.
architecture_rules.why: Logic in route handlers is hard to reuse and test, and ends up duplicated between routes.
architecture_rules.note: What counts as business logic cannot be told apart from plumbing by a pattern match.

architecture_rules.text: Every database change is a migration in supabase/migrations/.
architecture_rules.why: Migrations make the schema reproducible on every environment and give each change a rollback path; a change made by hand exists only on one database.
architecture_rules.note: Instruction only: no hook or CI step is invoked that flags schema changes made outside supabase/migrations/. The destructive-pattern guard of the migration flow is a separate rule.

migrations.prod: supabase db push --dry-run first, user confirms, then apply
